questions.q: Where does Databricks recommend starting GDPR and CCPA deletions in a medallion lakehouse?

options.t: By dropping and recreating every table each month
In gold, because that is what users query
In bronze, driven by a scheduled job over a table of deletion requests, then propagated
In silver only, because bronze is raw data and exempt from deletion requests

questions.explain: The GDPR page recommends deleting in bronze first, from a scheduled job that queries a control table of deletion requests, then propagating to silver and gold.

questions.q: A table has deletion vectors. After a DELETE of one user's rows, what else is needed to remove the data permanently?

options.t: `RESTORE` to the version before the DELETE
Nothing; DELETE removes it
`OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY (user_id)`, which rewrites the files without the deleted rows
`REORG TABLE ... APPLY (PURGE)`, then VACUUM after the retention period

questions.explain: For tables with deletion vectors, run REORG TABLE ... APPLY (PURGE) after deleting, then VACUUM to remove the old files.

questions.q: A streaming table reads a bronze Delta table, and rows are deleted from bronze for a GDPR request. What does Databricks recommend?

options.t: Delete in the source and the streaming table with DML, then read the source with skipChangeCommits
Convert the streaming table to an external table
Delete the stream's checkpoint
options.why: That reprocesses everything and doesn't delete.

options.t: Nothing: streaming tables apply deletes in their source automatically at the next update
options.why: Deletes in a streaming source break the stream.

questions.explain: Streaming tables process append-only data; an update or delete in the source breaks the stream. Delete in source and target, then use skipChangeCommits, or full refresh where history is cheap to reprocess.

questions.q: A materialized view reads a table from which a user's rows were deleted. What makes the deletion complete there?

options.t: A DELETE statement run on the materialized view itself, with the same predicate
options.why: Materialized views handle source deletes on refresh.

options.t: Refreshing the materialized view and running maintenance
Nothing at all; it was never stored
Dropping and recreating the view's catalog

questions.explain: Materialized views handle deletions in their sources automatically, but you must refresh them and run maintenance for the deletions to be fully processed.

questions.q: Which approach does the GDPR page call the safest?

options.t: Pseudonymizing identifiers in silver
options.why: The page calls complete erasure safest.

options.t: Masking PII columns for most users
Complete erasure of the PII
Encrypting the table with a customer-managed key

questions.explain: The page: obfuscation can use pseudonymization or masking, but the safest option is complete erasure, because eliminating re-identification risk often requires deleting the PII.

questions.q: Only the HR group may see full social security numbers. Which column mask expression fits?

options.t: `DENY SELECT (ssn) TO non_hr`
options.why: Unity Catalog SQL has no DENY statement.

options.t: `REVOKE SELECT (ssn) FROM all`
options.why: Column-level REVOKE isn't how masks work.

options.t: `CASE WHEN current_user() = 'hr' THEN ssn ELSE '***-**-****' END`
options.why: A group check, not a user name, is the documented pattern.

options.t: `CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('HR') THEN ssn ELSE '***-**-****' END`

questions.explain: A column mask is a SQL UDF returning the value or a masked one, often with is_account_group_member(); set with ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK.

questions.q: A row filter function returns FALSE for a row. What does a reader see?

options.t: Nothing: the row is hidden
The row with every column masked
An error
The row, flagged as filtered

questions.explain: A row filter is a SQL UDF evaluated per row at query time; rows where it returns FALSE are hidden.

questions.q: PII columns appear in hundreds of tables, including new ones each week. What does Databricks recommend for masking them consistently?

options.t: A column mask set by each table's owner when the table is created
options.why: That is per table and easily missed.

options.t: An ABAC policy that matches a governed tag such as PII
A dynamic view over every table
options.why: Views must be built and kept per table.

options.t: Granting SELECT only on views

questions.explain: ABAC policies use governed tags so new tagged columns are covered automatically, and table owners can't override them.

questions.q: Which statements about Databricks secrets are correct? (Choose two.)

options.t: Secret values are redacted in notebook output where possible
Anyone allowed to read a secret can still expose it, so grant carefully
Secret scopes should be created per person
options.why: Databricks recommends per role or application.

options.t: An Azure Key Vault-backed scope lets you write secrets from Databricks
Secrets can be stored safely in tag values

questions.explain: Secret scopes hold encrypted secrets with per-scope permissions; output is redacted where possible, but a reader can expose them. Key Vault-backed scopes are read-only.

questions.q: Why must tags never hold credentials or sensitive values?

options.t: Tag values are hashed
Tags are deleted after 30 days, so any credential in them is lost
Tags are stored as plain text and may be replicated globally
Tags are visible only to admins

questions.explain: The tags page warns that tag data is stored as plain text and may be replicated globally.

questions.q: In a clean room, what can a collaborator see of another party's tables?

options.t: Nothing at all, not even the schema
options.why: Column names and types are visible.

options.t: All rows of the shared tables, read-only, but no notebooks
A 10% sample
Column names and types, and the results of approved notebooks

questions.explain: Collaborators can't see each other's data but can see column names and types and run notebook code every collaborator has approved, in a central clean room.

questions.q: What do Clean Rooms require of each collaborator's workspace?

options.t: Serverless, Unity Catalog and OpenSharing enabled
Classic compute, the Hive metastore and a VPN between the parties
options.why: They need serverless and Unity Catalog.

options.t: Only a personal access token
A VPN to every other collaborator

questions.explain: Requirements: a workspace with serverless compute and Unity Catalog, and OpenSharing enabled for the metastore. Up to ten collaborators.

questions.q: A user can read a table's files directly from ADLS because it is an external table. Do its Unity Catalog row filters apply?

options.t: Yes, always
options.why: Direct file access bypasses Unity Catalog.

options.t: No: Unity Catalog privileges aren't enforced on direct file access
Only if the storage account sits behind a firewall that allows Databricks
Only for Parquet files

questions.explain: Unity Catalog privileges are not enforced on direct file access to external tables' files.

questions.q: On Azure, what is encrypted by default between worker nodes?

options.t: Only notebook results
Everything, always, with a customer-managed key that Databricks rotates
Traffic between workers isn't encrypted by default; it can be turned on (Premium)
Only shuffle files on disk

questions.explain: On Premium, encrypting traffic between worker nodes is available; it is not encrypted by default.
